topics.label: Introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the learning outcomes and historical approach for the lecture on cellular transformation and cancer genetics.

topics.label: Tumor virology, proto-oncogenes, and transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how the study of tumor viruses led to the identification of cellular proto-oncogenes and the development of assays to measure cellular transformation.

topics.label: Classification and genetics of oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how cancer mutations are classified and how allele dosage, the two-hit hypothesis, and dominant negative effects govern tumor suppressor and oncogene function.

topics.label: Mechanisms and cellular consequences of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular origins of sequence and chromosomal instability, detailing DNA repair pathways, replication and mitotic errors, and the resulting cellular stress responses.

topics.label: Multi-step tumor progression and hereditary cancer predisposition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how the stepwise accumulation of mutations drives cancer progression and how inherited genetic defects accelerate tumorigenesis.

topics.label: Conclusion and reading recommendations
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session, offers to answer questions, and recommends supplementary reading.
